# MTG Endophoric Reference Annotation

You read one Magic: The Gathering card and list every expression in its rules text that refers back to something else on the card (its **mentions**), with what each one refers to (its **antecedent**). Answer as a careful player who knows the game would explain the card to a friend.

Return your answer by calling the `StructuredOutput` tool once with the JSON object described in *Output fields*. Do not write the JSON as plain text.

## The three rules that matter most

1. **Find every mention.** Every occurrence of `it`, `its`, `itself`, `they`, `them`, `their`, `themselves`, `he`, `him`, `his`, `she`, `her` and `yourself` is a mention. There are no exceptions: not inside quoted abilities, not inside `as though ...`, `unless ...` or `if ...` clauses, and not when the antecedent sits in the same clause.
   - *"Players can't cast more than two spells each turn unless their hand is empty"* → `"their"` → `"Players"`.
   - *"This creature can block as though it had reach"* → `"it"` → `"This creature"`.
   - The one exception is a dummy `it` that refers to nothing: *"if it's your turn"*, *"if it's neither day nor night, it becomes day"*, *"if it's the second time"*. Reject it with reason `"expletive"`.
   The other kinds of mention (demonstratives, `"another"`, `"that much"`, `"if you do"` and the rest) are listed under *Kinds of mention*.

2. **Resolve by meaning.** The antecedent is whatever the expression actually refers to when the card is played. Where the expression sits in the text tells you nothing. Check each answer by putting your antecedent in place of the mention and reading the sentence again. If the result is not something the card could mean, the answer is wrong:
   - *"Tap all creatures with flying. Their controllers each draw a card."* Only permanents have controllers, so `"Their"` → `"all creatures with flying"`.
   - *"Spells you cast may be cast as though they had flash"*: spells have flash and players do not, so `"they"` → `"Spells you cast"`.
   - *"When this Aura leaves the battlefield, the creature it was attached to returns to its owner's hand"*: `"it"` → `"this Aura"`, since the Aura is what was attached, but `"its"` → `"the creature it was attached to"`, since the creature is what returns to its owner's hand. Two pronouns in one sentence can refer to different things, and a pronoun near a mention of the card itself need not mean the card.

3. **Say when you are unsure.** Set `confident: false` on any mention where you would hesitate if a friend asked "are you sure?". An `"uncertain"` verdict is cheap: it sends the card to a stronger reviewer, and that is what it is for. Set `confident: false` when any of these is true:
   - Two or more things on the card could be the antecedent and still make sense, even if you lean towards one.
   - A player and a group of objects both come before a `they`, `them` or `their`.
   - The mention is inside a quoted ability, or its antecedent is in a different ability.
   - You are not sure the expression refers back at all, or which span to quote.
   If any mention has `confident: false`, set `verdict: "uncertain"` and name those mentions and their candidate antecedents in `uncertainty_reason`. Otherwise set `verdict: "ok"` and `uncertainty_reason: null`. A card with no mentions is `"ok"`.

## Input

The card arrives as a name, a mana cost line labelled `[cost]` (or `[F<f>.cost]` on each face of a multi-face card), a type line, and one line per ability labelled `[A<n>]` (or `[F<f>.A<n>]`). Reminder text has been removed.
- A modal ability, a spree ability's `+ {cost} —` modes, and a die-roll result table are each a single ability.
- Level-up and station abilities start with a prefix such as `LEVEL 2-6 (3/3) | ` or `9+ | `. The prefix is part of the ability text but holds no mentions.
- The card refers to itself by its name, its short name (the part before a comma), or by `"this creature"`, `"this artifact"` and so on. On a multi-face card each face's name and short name refer to the card, and a face may name its other face (*"transform Henrika"*).
- Under an ability, a `quoted ability:` line repeats each quoted granted ability it contains, so you can see where quotes begin and end. It is not part of the card text.
- Under an ability, a `candidates:` line lists words and phrases that might be mentions, each with its occurrence number (`it#2` is the second whole-word `it` in that ability). The list is mechanical: it over-includes and can miss things. Handle every candidate one of two ways:
  - **annotate it**: list a mention in that ability whose phrase contains it, with the same occurrence number when the texts are equal (`it#2` → `mention_text: "it"`, `occurrence: 2`; `that#1` is covered by a mention `"that creature"`); or
  - **reject it** in `rejected`, with a few words saying why (`"self-reference"`, `"defining X"`, `"other than ..."`, `"numeral"`).
  Every pronoun candidate is a mention (rule 1), so never reject a pronoun, except a dummy `it` with reason `"expletive"`. Also list any mention that is not among the candidates. The card's own name and any leading label (*"Landfall — "*) are left out of the candidates.

## What is not a mention

These can be antecedents, but never list them as mentions:
- **The card itself**: its name or short name, and `this creature`, `this artifact`, `this enchantment`, `this spell`, `this card`, `this Aura`, `this Equipment`, `this Vehicle`, `this permanent`, `this land`, `this Saga`, `this Class`, `this Case`, `this Room`, `this door`, `this Spacecraft`, `this Siege`, `this battle`.
- **Inside a quoted ability**, `this creature` (or `this <type>`) means the object that *has* the ability, while the card's own name still means the card that *grants* it. Neither is a mention, and a pronoun inside the quotes can refer to either: on an Equipment named Glint Rod, in *Equipped creature has "{T}: It deals 1 damage to any target. Return Glint Rod to its owner's hand"*, `"It"` is the equipped creature and `"its"` is Glint Rod.
- **`this ability`.**
- **`you` and `your`.** They are not mentions, but `you` can be the antecedent of `yourself`.
- **Attachment hosts**: `enchanted creature`, `enchanted permanent`, `enchanted land`, `enchanted player`, `equipped creature`, `fortified land`.
- **The current moment**: `this turn`, `this phase`, `this step`, `this combat`, `this game`, and `this one` in *"after this one"*. (`that turn` is a mention.)
- **Fixed game things**: `the battlefield`, `the stack`, `the command zone`, `the exile zone`, `the top card of your library`, `the top N cards of your library`, `the bottom of your library`, `the number of ...`, `the end of turn`, `the beginning of ...`, `the monarch`, `the initiative`.
- **Flavor words and mode labels**: the words before a ` — ` that name an ability or a mode, such as *"Landfall — "* or a mode *"• Charge Them — "*. They have no rules meaning, so nothing in them is a mention, and they are left out of the candidates.
- **Relative `that`** (*"a creature that attacked"*) and verb phrases with no surface pronoun (*"gets +1/+0 and can't be blocked"*).

## Kinds of mention (`category`)

- **`pronoun`**: `it`, `its`, `they`, `them`, `their`, `he`, `him`, `his`, `she`, `her`, and `one` when it stands for a noun (*"for each one"*). For a possessive, list only the pronoun: in `its controller` the mention is `"its"`. A plural pronoun that refers to several separately named things takes `kind: "split"` (*"Tap target creature and target artifact. Untap them at your next upkeep"* → `"target creature + target artifact"`).
- **`reflexive`**: `itself`, `themselves`, `yourself`.
- **`demonstrative`**: `that <noun>`, `those <noun>`, joined forms (`that player or permanent`), `that turn`, and `this mana` (antecedent: the mana the ability adds, such as `"{G}{G}"`). For a possessive, list only the noun phrase: `"that creature"` in `that creature's controller`. `that cost` after a cost-changing clause → that clause, `referent_type: "outcome_or_amount"`.
- **`definite_readback`**: a `the <noun>` that picks out something already introduced, such as `the token`, `the creature you control`, `the chosen <noun>`, `the last chosen <noun>`, `the total`, `the difference`, `the vote` and `the copy`. When the thing was introduced by a verb rather than a noun phrase, the antecedent is that clause: `the copy` → `"Copy that spell"`, `the difference` → the comparison clause, `the vote` → the voting clause.
- **`participial_description`**: a noun phrase built on an earlier action, such as `the exiled card`, `the sacrificed creature`, `the card revealed this way`, or `cards exiled with this artifact` / `the creature put onto the battlefield with this Aura` (the whole noun phrase is the mention). The antecedent is the object acted on, which may be in an additional cost or in another ability of the card that performs the action.
- **`contrastive`**: `another` or `other` with no printed `than ...`. The antecedent is what is excluded. Use `kind: "source"` (with `ability` and `text` null) when that is the card itself and the card is not named in this ability, `kind: "performer"` (with `ability` and `text` null) when it is `you`, and `kind: "distributive_member"` when each member of a plural subject is excluded from its own count (*"Creatures you control get +1/+1 for each [other] creature you control"* → `"Creatures you control"`). After *"... loses all other abilities"*, `other` excludes the abilities just granted.
- **`complement_or_reciprocal`**: `the rest` and `the other` (antecedent `text`: the selected part, `secondary_text`: the whole collection), and reciprocal `each other` and `one another` at the end of a phrase (*"those creatures fight each other"*; antecedent: the plural subject). `each other creature` is not reciprocal: there `other` is `contrastive`.
- **`amount_or_outcome`**: `that much` and `that many` (antecedent: the clause that produced the amount), and each use of a variable `X`, `Y` or `Z` in rules text. A variable's antecedent is `"{X}"` in the mana cost (`ability: "cost"`), `"{X}"` in an ability's cost (that ability), or the `"where X is ..."` clause. Do not list `{X}` in a cost, or the `X` in `where X is`, as a mention.
- **`lookback_or_followup`**: expressions that refer back to an action, condition or effect, such as `this way`, `if you do`, `if you don't`, `when you do`, `otherwise`, `this` in *"Do this only once each turn"*, `this process`, `this effect` and `the same` in *"The same is true for ..."*. Use `referent_type: "event_or_action"`, with the clause as the antecedent. In *"If the player does"*, annotate both the lookback `"If the player does"` and, separately, `"the player"` (a `definite_readback` for the player named earlier).
- **`relative`**: `which`, `who`, `whose`, `whom` (antecedent: the noun phrase they modify).

## Span rules (machine-checked: a violation sends the card for repair)

1. **Verbatim.** `antecedent.text`, `antecedent.secondary_text` and `context_snippet` (without its brackets) are copied character for character from the card, with the same capitals and punctuation. `antecedent.text` comes from the ability named in `antecedent.ability`, or from the mana cost (`"cost"` or `"F<f>.cost"`). `secondary_text` may come from any ability. The only joined form is `kind: "split"`, whose parts are each verbatim and are joined with `" + "`. When a split's parts are in different abilities, `antecedent.ability` lists one ability per part in the same order, joined the same way (`"A0 + A1"`).
2. **First mention.** In a chain of references to one thing, `antecedent.text` is the phrase that first introduced it, never another mention. *"Reveal a card at random from your hand, then put that card on top of your library. Its owner gains 1 life."* → both `"that card"` and `"Its"` have `text: "a card at random from your hand"`. If a step picks a new subset from a group (*"... choose a creature card from among them. Put that card ..."*), the subset phrase introduces a new thing.
3. **Clauses.** When the antecedent is an action, event or amount, quote the clause from its subject or verb. Leave out a leading `When`, `Whenever`, `At`, `If`, `Then` or `and`, but keep `you may`: *"... you may pay {2}. If you do, ..."* → `"you may pay {2}"`. Keep the card's capitals: at the start of a sentence the span is `"You may pay {2}"`.
4. **`occurrence`** is the position of `mention_text` among **all** whole-word, case-insensitive matches in that ability, counting left to right. Count matches you are not annotating too: the `X` in `{X}` and in `where X is`, `this` in `this creature`, and `one` in `one mana`. `it` does not match inside `its` or `itself`, but it does match inside `it's`.

## Output fields

- `card_name`: the card's exact name.
- `verdict`, `uncertainty_reason`: see rule 3.
- `mentions`: in reading order. Each has:
  - `ability`, `mention_text`, `occurrence`.
  - `context_snippet`: a short verbatim piece of the ability with the mention in brackets, e.g. `"lose life equal to [its] mana value"`.
  - `category`: from *Kinds of mention*.
  - `antecedent`:
    - `kind`: `"text_span"` (the antecedent is quoted from the card), `"split"`, `"source"`, `"performer"` or `"distributive_member"` (see `contrastive`).
    - `referent_type`: `"object"` (cards, spells, permanents, tokens, mana, piles), `"player"`, `"event_or_action"`, `"outcome_or_amount"` (a number, an amount or a cost), `"choice"` (a chosen color, type, name or number, but not a chosen player or object), or `"turn"`.
    - `ability`, `text`: where the antecedent is and what it says. Both are null only for `"source"` and `"performer"`.
    - `secondary_text`: null unless one of these applies:
      - for `the rest` or `the other`, the whole collection;
      - for `participial_description`, the action clause;
      - when the referent was re-mentioned, or changed zones, between its first mention and this one, the latest such re-mention (*"... then put that card on top of your library. Its owner gains 1 life"* → for `"Its"`, `"put that card on top of your library"`);
      - for a pronoun inside a quoted ability that refers to the object having the ability, the `"this creature"` inside the quotes.
  - `confident`: see rule 3.
- `rejected`: every candidate you decided is not a mention, each as `{"ability": "A0", "candidate": "one", "occurrence": 1, "reason": "numeral"}`. Use `[]` when there is none.

Example (an invented card):

```
Card: Example Card
[cost] Mana Cost: {1}{U}
Type Line: Sorcery
Abilities:
[A0] Reveal four cards from the top of your library. Choose one of them to put into your hand, then shuffle the rest into your library. If that card is a land card, you may put it onto the battlefield instead.
    candidates: one#1, them#1, the rest#1, that card#1, it#1
```

```json
{
  "card_name": "Example Card",
  "verdict": "ok",
  "uncertainty_reason": null,
  "rejected": [{"ability": "A0", "candidate": "one", "occurrence": 1, "reason": "quantifier, part of \"one of them\""}],
  "mentions": [
    {"ability": "A0", "mention_text": "them", "occurrence": 1, "context_snippet": "Choose one of [them] to put into your hand",
     "category": "pronoun",
     "antecedent": {"kind": "text_span", "referent_type": "object", "ability": "A0", "text": "four cards from the top of your library", "secondary_text": null},
     "confident": true},
    {"ability": "A0", "mention_text": "the rest", "occurrence": 1, "context_snippet": "then shuffle [the rest] into your library",
     "category": "complement_or_reciprocal",
     "antecedent": {"kind": "text_span", "referent_type": "object", "ability": "A0", "text": "one of them", "secondary_text": "four cards from the top of your library"},
     "confident": true},
    {"ability": "A0", "mention_text": "that card", "occurrence": 1, "context_snippet": "If [that card] is a land card",
     "category": "demonstrative",
     "antecedent": {"kind": "text_span", "referent_type": "object", "ability": "A0", "text": "one of them", "secondary_text": null},
     "confident": true},
    {"ability": "A0", "mention_text": "it", "occurrence": 1, "context_snippet": "you may put [it] onto the battlefield",
     "category": "pronoun",
     "antecedent": {"kind": "text_span", "referent_type": "object", "ability": "A0", "text": "one of them", "secondary_text": "that card"},
     "confident": true}
  ]
}
```

On a card where `"it"` could equally be read as one of two things, that mention would have `confident: false`, the verdict would be `"uncertain"`, and `uncertainty_reason` would name both candidates.
